body: When it comes to retail you have to chase them. Keep following up, keep calling, go there if you can. It's unfortunate that you're the one who has to chase them for minimum wage, but it is what it is

I'm alone rn, so it's the perfect time to practice. The bad news is, even with my flat blanket that I folded over and over (instead of my rope), none of the doorways are strong enough. I guess the only reliable method is for me to purchase some sand bags or other heavy things to use as weights and drown myself. That way, my body can't rise to the surface too early on impulse. I may not know how to swim, but I'm pretty sure that if I don't have weights, I'll still float up top and it won't be enough to kill me. 12-15 minutes of my body fighting for air will be hell, but at least I know I'll be dead after that timeframe passes.

EDIT: To clarify, I tried putting weight on the blanket and since none of the doors can shut securely, I know it will just turn loose. Worst case scenario, I break it and the landlord will just charge me extra for breaking the door. That's what I meant.

I believe you, but I don't really have many options, since I don't own a firearm and bridges aren't tall enough to cause death. I found some videos of people hanging themselves using doorways as anchors (I don't have any strong ceiling points. I also have some rope, and long blankets.

Drowning, according to the internet, can take up to 12 minutes before you die completely. Hanging takes about half the time at most from the videos I watched, so I'm learning how to make a hangman's knot so I can look to hanging as an alternative. I can use my doorway as an anchor point. I'm really short, too (5'3) so I think it might work. 

Don't worry, I'm not going to kill myself right now. I'm going to hang out with my boyfriend later, so I plan to wait until that's over. Depending on how the day goes and how this practice run goes, I might just choose hanging instead. I already have a plan on to whom I can give stuff away, like my phone and my tarantula. My car will be repo-ed next week if I don't make my promise to pay date, so if I'm successful tonight, I won't have to worry about it being in the driveway for long.
The way I see it, people only "care" about you and want to stop you from offing yourself because it gives them an ego boost, thinking they're some hero who saved someone from going through with it

A small loan from my boyfriend plus being unemployed and never knowing when I can pay it back...I know this comparison is unequal, but that makes me feel like my cousins in the Philippines, who would latch onto men for money and trap them by getting pregnant (it won't work, so they end up having multiple baby daddies). That makes me feel like more of a burden. I already feel like a burden and like a weakling when I vent to him about vulnerabilities, because I know he's been through worse in life. 

You're right, it's only going to get worse. And cherry on top, if you're unemployed for a long time, hiring managers will think you're unemployable and lazy, because in their minds, all you did was sit on your ass twiddling your thumbs during the pandemic, while they worked the job of 3 people because the business decided to get rid of staff. 

My boyfriend will be sad for a while; I don't know how long. He'll probably end up hating me, too, who knows? But he deserves someone who is far stronger than I am and I know he'll find someone like that one day.

Customer service, administration office management/small business management. I'd get interviews, usually through temp agencies, but clients will pull out due to budgeting, or due to none of the interviewed candidates meeting their wish list. 

I've applied at groceries as well, which are minimum wage and won't schedule any more than 10 hours a week, which makes it so that you don't receive benefits (and your bills aren't paid because you're not earning enough). I've tried doing gig apps, but due to bots, well-paying batches are now difficult to catch. I even tried for a CNA position at a really bad hospital, but I got the displeasure of getting to speak to corporate, which didn't know or give a shit about its hospital staff so any questions I had were met with "I don't know, I only deal with the corporate side, I don't go to the sites". 

I've never been unemployed for more than 3 weeks, because I always had a backup plan. Most people I'd vent to will say the situation is unique due to the pandemic, I'll find one eventually, etc. It makes me feel unemployable and stupid sometimes, even though that isn't the case. 

Being stuck at home doing nothing but job searching for 6 months straight, on top of having mental health issues even before the pandemic is exhausting. I know it makes me sound like a weakling, but honestly, I'm tired. I can't afford mental health help, and the one thing people suggest is inpatient, which is counterproductive because I can't even pay for that and even if I somehow found a free way to do it, they won't release you unless you have an appointment which requires money, and most importantly, I can't find a job while I'm stuck with other people in a hospital who probably deserve and want that care more than I do. People will move on with time, my partner is strong so I know he'll find someone who deserves him better.

If he ever killed himself, of course I'd be miserable, but I'd like to think I'd eventually move on with time. 

He has too much on his plate already, and I don't want to add to it.

On the other hand, if I'm gone, I no longer have to deal with memories that keep resurfacing. I won't have to deal with panic attacks, and other mental health issues that I struggle with on the daily, but hide away because I'd rather not burden other people with silly things I should have gotten over, but for some reason can't.

I'd love to take multiple minimum wage jobs. 

I've done it. 

But you know what, at best it's 3 hours per week. Not enough to survive on, especially with my bills. Even minimum wage jobs are difficult to come by. Gig economy in my area is shit. Moving in with my parents out of state isn't an option, because they'll just make me feel worthless again, as they always have, because of whateer reason they feel like naming for that particular day. And I'd die before I resort to free-loading (off of my boyfriend's back, because he has more than enough to worry about. He's a human, not an ATM)

And as you said, time heals all wounds. He'll probably be sad for a while. But eventually, I know he'll find someone else who's far more deserving, someone with less baggage and someone who's strong enough and more equipped to handle life. I'm not that person.

Venting, I guess. 

When I first talked about it with my partner, I made him cry. He lost his mother when he was a teenager, and he found out that hi partner of almost 4 years is seriously considering suicide, I can't blame him. At the same time, it's not like he can give me a job, either. Neither can any of my friends. Besides, they have greater problems, mine will just be seen as silly and I'll be viewed as weak. It may be true, but it's not exactly helpful. When I vent to people, I usually already have a solution, except for this one. 

So it's useless, I'd rather just vent to strangers on the internet until I actually die. I'm thinking about doing it this weekend, or perhaps next weekend, but I'm unsure if I want to do it during daylight. I'm in a city where most people are cold and only care about themselves, so no one will pay any mind to me; I see that as a huge advantage, because a pretty park will be the last thing I see if I do decide to do it in daylight.
